suggested_rewrite: Computing r = x / y without guarding against |y| ≈ 0; for small y this amplifies error unboundedly. Use log(x) - log(y) directly (with branch handling) or check |y| against a tolerance before forming the ratio.
x / y can blow up when y is near zero; prefer log|x| - log|y| to avoid forming the ratio, which both prevents overflow/underflow and reduces error amplification.
log(kAbs(r)) where r = x/y suffers cancellation when |r| ≈ 1 (i.e. x ≈ y); use log1p(|r|-1) computed from a stable expression, or log|x| - log|y|, to preserve precision near the branch.
